title: 同相放大器：反馈里放两个电阻
summary: 把跟随器的反馈线换成 RF 22 kΩ 和 RG 10 kΩ：输出变成输入的好几倍。用电位器逐点测增益，再把输入调大，看输出顶到头。
description: 同相放大器：电位器给 IN+ 一个 0–9 V 的直流电压（10% ≈ 0.9 V），输出经 RF、RG 分压后送回 IN−。虚短（V(IN−) = V(IN+)）和虚断（输入不取电流）给出 Vo = (1 + RF/RG) × Vi。输出超出 0 … V+ − 1.5 V 时就饱和，虚短不再成立。

cards.title: 跟随器，但反馈打了折
text: 从 2.5 的跟随器出发，IN+ 接电位器 **RV1** `10 kΩ`（1 脚接 GND，3 脚接 +9 V）。
把 OUT–IN− 那根线换掉：**RF** `22 kΩ` 从 OUT 接到 IN−，**RG** `10 kΩ` 从 IN− 接到 GND。
旋钮拨到 `10%`，测 **IN+** 和 **OUT** 对 GND 的电压。
输出是输入的几倍？

cards.title: 输出必须把 IN− 抬到 IN+ 那么高
text: - RF 和 RG 从 OUT 到 GND 组成一个分压器。IN− 在中间，只拿到输出的一部分：$\frac{R_G}{R_F + R_G}$。
- op-amp（运算放大器）会一直推，直到 IN− 等于 IN+（虚短）。所以输出必须比输入大，大的倍数正好是这个比例的倒数。
![](fig:amp)
- 用电流说也一样：IN− 不取电流（虚断），RG 里的电流 $V_{in}/R_G$ 全部也流过 RF。两段电压加起来：
$$V_o = \left(1 + \frac{R_F}{R_G}\right) V_{in}$$
- 如果 RF = RG = 10 kΩ，增益就是 $1 + 10/10 = 2$。用 RF = 22 kΩ 算出你的增益，再预测 `10%`、`20%`、`50%` 时的 OUT。别忘了 V+ − 1.5 V 的天花板。

cards.title: 逐点测，直到顶到头
text: - 每次都测 **IN+**、**IN−**、**OUT** 对 GND 的电压。
- 在 `20%` 时把电流表先串进 **RG**、再串进 **RF**：电流一样吗？
- 电路检查通过后填测量题。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **同相放大器**：$V_o = (1 + R_F/R_G)\,V_{in}$，和输入同号，增益不小于 1。
- 虚短只在输出没出范围时成立。一饱和，IN− 就追不上 IN+，公式失效。
- 从外面看，带反馈的 op-amp（运算放大器）就是一个**电压控制电压源**：一个数值由另一个电压决定的电源。这就是理论题里的受控源。
- 坑：真实的 LM358 **输入端**也最好低于约 V+ − 1.5 V。这个电位器转过约 `83%`，真实芯片就不可靠了；仿真没有模拟这一点。

caption.text: V_in 接 IN+。同一个电流 I 从输出经 RF、RG 流到 GND；IN− 拿到输出的 RG / (RF + RG)。

i18n.en: V_in drives IN+. One current I flows from the output through RF and RG to GND; IN− gets RG / (RF + RG) of the output.

en.startNote: **Half-built**: the LM358 is seated and powered (lesson 14), and the pot is wired as a 0–9 V input with its wiper on pin 3 IN+. **Why**: the gain is set by the feedback network — that is what this lab is about. **Your job**: add RF (22kΩ, pin 1 OUT → pin 2 IN−) and RG (10kΩ, pin 2 IN− → GND).
en.title: The non-inverting amplifier: two resistors in the feedback
en.summary: Replace the follower's feedback wire with RF 22 kΩ and RG 10 kΩ: the output becomes several times the input. Measure the gain with a pot, then turn the input up and watch the output hit the ceiling.
en.description: Non-inverting amplifier: a pot gives IN+ a DC voltage of 0–9 V (10% ≈ 0.9 V), and the output comes back to IN− through the RF–RG divider. The virtual short (V(IN−) = V(IN+)) and virtual open (no input current) give Vo = (1 + RF/RG) × Vi. Outside 0 … V+ − 1.5 V the output saturates and the virtual short no longer holds.
en.compare:
**Compare**: gain Vo = Vi + RF × Vi / RG = (1 + 22/10) Vi = **3.2 Vi**.
- 10%: Vi ≈ 0.90 V → Vo ≈ **2.88 V**, and IN− is 0.90 V too (virtual short).
- 20%: Vi ≈ 1.80 V → Vo ≈ **5.76 V**; RG's current = 1.80 / 10k = 0.18 mA, and RF carries 0.18 mA as well.
- 50%: Vi = 4.50 V → 14.4 V in theory, but the output tops out at V+ − 1.5 V = **7.5 V**: clipped (saturated). IN− is then 7.5 × 10 / 32 ≈ 2.34 V, no longer equal to IN+.

3.2 × 4.5 = 14.4 V in theory, but the LM358 output tops out at V+ − 1.5 V ≈ 7.5 V: saturated (clipped).

Pot: pin 1 to GND, pin 3 to +9 V, the middle wiper to IN+ (pin 3). Wired the other way, the knob turns backwards.

cards.title: A follower with a discounted feedback
text: Start from the follower of 2.5, with pot **RV1** `10 kΩ` on IN+ (pin 1 to GND, pin 3 to +9 V).
Replace the OUT–IN− wire: **RF** `22 kΩ` from OUT to IN−, and **RG** `10 kΩ` from IN− to GND.
Set the knob to `10%` and measure **IN+** and **OUT** against GND.
How many times larger is the output than the input?

cards.title: The output must lift IN− up to IN+
text: - RF and RG form a divider from OUT down to GND. IN− sits at its middle and only gets a fraction of the output: $\frac{R_G}{R_F + R_G}$.
- The op-amp keeps pushing until IN− equals IN+ (virtual short). So the output has to be larger than the input by exactly the inverse of that fraction.
![](fig:amp)
- Same story with currents: IN− takes no current (virtual open), so the current through RG, $V_{in}/R_G$, all flows through RF too. Adding up the two voltage drops:
$$V_o = \left(1 + \frac{R_F}{R_G}\right) V_{in}$$
- With RF = RG = 10 kΩ the gain would be $1 + 10/10 = 2$. Work out yours with RF = 22 kΩ, then predict OUT at `10%`, `20%` and `50%`. Mind the ceiling at V+ − 1.5 V.

cards.title: Point by point, up to the ceiling
text: - Turn the knob to `10%`, `20%` and `50%`.
- Each time, measure **IN+**, **IN−** and **OUT** against GND.
- At `20%`, put the ammeter in series with **RG**, then with **RF**: same current?
- Once the circuit check passes, fill in the questions.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Non-inverting amplifier**: $V_o = (1 + R_F/R_G)\,V_{in}$, same sign as the input. Gain at least 1.
- The virtual short holds only while the output is inside its range. Saturated, IN− falls behind IN+ and the formula stops.
- To the outside, an op-amp with feedback is a **voltage-controlled voltage source**: a source whose value is set by another voltage. That is the dependent source of the theory chapter.
- Pitfall: a real LM358 also wants its **inputs** below about V+ − 1.5 V. Above about `83%` on this pot a real chip misbehaves; the simulator doesn't model that.
